paras: The attempted lynching of Grant Alexander took place in June 1888, when a Black man jailed on a charge of assaulting a white woman in Boughton township was the target of several failed attempts to lynch him. Black residents guarded the jail each night to protect him, and the local paper criticized the sheriffs for relying on a guard of Black men while also opposing lynch law.

According to the Nevada County picayune, Alexander, whom it called "a negro," was accused of assaulting "a white lady" in Boughton township during the week before its June 27 issue. The paper wrote that he "was foiled in his hellish intent," stating the accusation as fact.

Alexander was captured, identified and bound over by the examining court, and a number of Prescott residents traveled to Boughton on the Friday before June 27 to attend his preliminary trial. "Several attempts were made to lynch him but failed," the paper reported, without detail. Black residents surrounded the jail every night to protect him, and the paper reported fears that the "vigilantes" and the guard would come into conflict.

On Saturday night Sheriffs Regan and Greer placed a guard of Black men about the jail. By the time of the report, Alexander was said to be in "the state penetentiary, for safe keeping," though the paper does not explain how this fits with the jail guard.
The paper noted "severe strictures" upon the sheriffs for placing the guard. No report of a later trial, verdict or sentence appears in the coverage.

The only coverage found is two local paragraphs in the June 27, 1888, Nevada County picayune. Its editor called it "ill-advised" to have formed the guard "of negroes" and placed them "in an attitude of defying" the "outraged white citizens," but commended the officers for protecting prisoners and county property. The column closed by insisting that "Judge Lynch" should not be permitted to override established law once legal proceedings had begun.
A second item in the same issue listed "the state vs. Grant Alexander, (col.)" among routine social notes.
